question.problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{5}{13},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{12}{13},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Given that $v$ lies in the fourth quadrant, then

| $\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)$ | $=$ | {{field-1}}$\,\,+\,$ {{field-2}}$\sqrt{7}$ | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | $52$ |  |
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u$, $\operatorname{cos}⁡u$, and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡v,$ we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v=1\,⟹\,{sin}^{2}⁡v=1-{cos}^{2}⁡v
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡v & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡v \\  & =1-{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{3}^{2}}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{9}{16} \\  & =\frac{16}{16}-\frac{9}{16} \\  & =\frac{7}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{7}{16}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $v$ lies in the fourth quadrant, where sine is negative. So, we disregard the positive value, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡v=-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}.
$$

We can now apply the difference formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{5}{13})(\frac{3}{4})-(\frac{12}{13})(-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{15}{52}+\frac{12\sqrt{7}}{52} \\  & =\frac{15+12\sqrt{7}}{52}\end{aligned}
$$
